subject: science
title: Gases and the properties of water

cards.back: The idea that everything is made of tiny particles that are too small to see.
cards.say: particle model. The idea that everything is made of tiny particles that are too small to see.

cards.back: Packed closely in a regular pattern. They only vibrate in place.
cards.say: particles in a solid. Packed closely in a regular pattern. They only vibrate in place.

cards.back: Close together but not in a pattern. They slide past each other.
cards.say: particles in a liquid. Close together but not in a pattern. They slide past each other.

cards.back: Far apart and moving quickly in all directions.
cards.say: particles in a gas. Far apart and moving quickly in all directions.

cards.front: Why can a gas be squashed into a smaller space?
cards.back: Its particles are far apart, so they can be pushed closer together.
cards.say: Why can a gas be squashed into a smaller space? Its particles are far apart, so they can be pushed closer together.

cards.front: Why is it hard to squash a liquid or a solid?
cards.back: Their particles are already close together.
cards.say: Why is it hard to squash a liquid or a solid? Their particles are already close together.

cards.front: Why does a gas fill its container?
cards.back: Its particles move freely in all directions until they spread out everywhere.
cards.say: Why does a gas fill its container? Its particles move freely in all directions until they spread out everywhere.

cards.front: Why does a solid keep its shape?
cards.back: Its particles are held in fixed places and cannot move past each other.
cards.say: Why does a solid keep its shape? Its particles are held in fixed places and cannot move past each other.

cards.back: A gas that turns limewater milky. It is used to make drinks fizzy.
cards.say: carbon dioxide. A gas that turns limewater milky. It is used to make drinks fizzy.

cards.back: The lightest gas. It burns with a squeaky pop.
cards.say: hydrogen. The lightest gas. It burns with a squeaky pop.

cards.back: A very light gas that does not burn. It is used to fill balloons.
cards.say: helium. A very light gas that does not burn. It is used to fill balloons.

cards.front: What does pure water look like and taste like?
cards.back: Colourless, with no taste and no smell.
cards.say: What does pure water look like and taste like? Colourless, with no taste and no smell.

cards.front: What happens to water when it freezes?
cards.back: It expands. Ice takes up more space than the same mass of liquid water.
cards.say: What happens to water when it freezes? It expands. Ice takes up more space than the same mass of liquid water.

cards.front: Why does ice float on water?
cards.back: Ice is less dense than liquid water, because it expands as it freezes.
cards.say: Why does ice float on water? Ice is less dense than liquid water, because it expands as it freezes.

cards.front: Why is water called a good solvent?
cards.back: It can dissolve many different substances.
cards.say: Why is water called a good solvent? It can dissolve many different substances.

cards.back: Yes. Air has mass. A balloon full of air has more mass than an empty one.
cards.say: Do gases have mass? Yes. Air has mass. A balloon full of air has more mass than an empty one.

cards.front: Why can you smell cooking from another room?
cards.back: Gas particles move and spread out until they mix with the air everywhere.
cards.say: Why can you smell cooking from another room? Gas particles move and spread out until they mix with the air everywhere.

cards.front: What happens to a gas when it is heated?
cards.back: Its particles move faster and the gas expands.
cards.say: What happens to a gas when it is heated? Its particles move faster and the gas expands.

cards.front: Do liquids have a fixed volume?
cards.back: Yes. A liquid keeps the same volume but takes the shape of its container.
cards.say: Do liquids have a fixed volume? Yes. A liquid keeps the same volume but takes the shape of its container.
